selected_model.ood_2020_note: 2020 was treated as a separate out-of-distribution (OOD) stress test due to the COVID-19 shelter-in-place demand collapse (-87.1% in April 2020 vs. April 2019) and 13 newly opened Sherman stations. While XGBoost won Validation 2018, Main Test 2019 (all metrics), cold-start Sherman stations (R²=+0.242), and 24h-ahead OOD 2020, Random Forest slightly outperformed the deeper 1h-ahead XGBoost model on overall 2020 OOD RMSE (0.2661 vs. 0.2696).
selected_model.selection_criterion: Lowest Validation 2018 RMSE (strictly chronological; 2019 kept untouched until final retrain on 2011-2018)

operational_evaluation.honest_findings: Distribution-propagated Erlang-B accounts for non-linear Jensen's inequality effects where E[B(c, lambda)] > B(c, E[lambda]) in volatile hours, improving probabilistic calibration and providing calibrated uncertainty bounds for driver journey planning.

recommendations.disclaimer: Planning Suggestion Only: The City of Palo Alto dataset does not include verified station port capacities, real-time operational port counts, queue lengths, turn-aways, or maintenance logs. Recommendations reflect historical and predicted session arrival patterns and must not be interpreted as confirmed congestion, utilization percentages, or definitive infrastructure requirements.
